messages.text: Hi there — I'm Sarah, an AI researcher with HeliumDeploy. Thank you so much for taking 25 minutes to do this — it really means a lot. Honestly, the more you can share with me, the better — we're aiming for about fifteen hundred words of feedback together, so please don't worry about going long. The founders read every word of these chats, so what you say actually shapes what HD does next. As a thank-you you'll get a $75 discount code at the end. So — to kick us off, tell me about your mining setup right now. What are you running, where, and what are you trying to figure out next?

Currently, I'm running nine BitX uh, standard and BitX Gamma machines, and I'm running two nano three s machines, and I'm running one nerd Oct x twelve terahash machine for a total of about thirty eight terahash machines. I'm currently mining at home. But I'm looking to branch out. I've got an idea that I've actually pursued even further as for a website and things of that sort where I want to offer some services to people in regards to mining subscriptions. So I'll be in the market for more machines, and, uh, we'll possibly be moving into a retail not retail. I'm sorry. A commercial location to better provide myself with power and the services I need to provide these services.

Whoa, okay — that's a serious fleet. Nine Bitaxes, two Nano 3S, a NerdOctaxe at 12 TH — you're deep in this. And now you're spinning up a subscription service on top of it? Tell me more about that — what does the service actually look like for the customer? Like, what are they paying for?

Uh, without trying to release a lot of my idea, I would be offering I would be offering a service where people that can't afford to spend money on minors and can't afford to or don't want to uh, take the time to know how to keep an eye on the machines, know when firm or firmware needs to be updated, Uh, they can order subscription to a specific minor. And if that minor hits a block, they'll share in the profit of that block hit on that miner.

Got it — so basically shared-lottery solo mining as a managed service. People buy in, you handle the ops, they get a cut if their machine hits. That's clever.

So a couple things I want to dig into. First — you're already running 12 units at home in Vegas. How are you handling the heat and power right now, before the commercial move? Like, what room are they in, and what's your electric bill looking like?

I have a dedicated room for the, uh, machines right now, so, uh, I'm able to keep that room nice and cool, uh, even though the heat does fill the room up. I have an additional, uh, AC system inside that room. I, uh, as far as electric bill, I've only been doing this now less than a month, so I don't have a current, uh, cost on that, but I'm estimating my cost right now will be approximately fifty to seventy dollars in electrical cost. Uh, we do have lower electrical costs here as far as homes go. So I, uh, I don't I don't anticipate spending more than forty to fifty dollars a month on my current setup.

Less than a month in and you've already got 12 units, a dedicated cooled room, AND a subscription business plan? That's a fast ramp. What got you here that fast — what were you doing right before this, and what flipped the switch?

I've been investing in stocks and investing in some cryptocurrency, and have always been interested in mining, but never went forward with it until I found the home miners that are available because it would be hard for me to sell a subscription service to a hundred and twenty Terahash machine. Uh, the the the cost would be astronomical. And, uh, so I I'm trying to make my subscription service affordable to all. Uh, I currently am semi retired, from a position I've held for thirty years and have a decent income, decent retirement, I travel out the country a lot. So I do have a partner that will be in this business with me once I get it going. But, uh, that's where I currently am. I even though I'm semi retired, I work eighty to a hundred and twenty hours a week. Doing what I do in Vegas.

Wow, semi-retired and working 120-hour weeks — that's a particular kind of "retired." Respect. And it makes total sense now — you wanted in on mining, but you needed a unit economics story that works at the consumer subscription price point, not industrial. Home miners gave you that.

Let me pull up what you've been buying so I can ground this — give me a sec. So — when you were picking the units for the fleet, how did you land on the Bitaxe Gamma + Nano 3S + NerdOctaxe mix specifically? Walk me through that decision — were you looking at this NerdQaxe 6.1 too, or did you skip it?

At first, I started with the BitX, uh, just the standard one point two terahash machines. Uh, I found a company online. It was not Helium Deploy, but I've heard a lot about Helium Deploy, and, uh, your prices are really good. So I will be making the switch to buying units from you. But, uh, uh, I started with the bit standard bid ax and went to bid ax Gamma one point six terahash machines. Uh, I then went with the, uh, nano three s six terahash machines. Got two of them. Then I eventually progressed over the last thirty days into the twelve Terahash node oct x. Now I have purchased a majority of these machines through a different vendor, but that vendor has not been able to provide me with the service that I'm looking for. Along shipping dates, along uh, waits for everything. And their prices are now not too good. Now that I found Helium Deploy and I've actually per some of my bid ax machines and one of my nano three s from uh, actually, uh, Amazon. No. I'm sorry. Yeah. Amazon. And, uh, got better pricing than the current person I was using or company I was using. But, again, Helium Deploy after finding the site, actually is providing much more of a price point better price point for me and my goals that I wanna meet.

Okay — so you came up the ladder: Bitaxe standard → Gamma → Nano 3S → NerdOctaxe. And you've been buying from another vendor (plus some on Amazon) but the service was bad and now you're switching to HD for the price. Got it.

Two things I want to dig into. First — which vendor were you using before that let you down? And second — when you say service, what specifically went wrong? Like, was it a shipping thing, a DOA, a support thing?

Uh, the previous vendor that I've been using is Bitcoin March. And, uh, the exact problem that I've been having is their uh, uh, how should I say, Their inability for all of their staff to be giving me the correct information One person will give me information on shipping, uh, then another one will email me say, oh, that person was wrong. Uh, when they had a special event a few of their people had to go to. They put someone in charge of their shipping department. So that that person could go to the show and, uh, they basically put someone in charge that didn't know what he was doing, didn't know what he was talking about. So uh, I guess you would say I have a problem with their management of their staff. And their shipping times. The printed shipping label It'll show printed on the uh, UPS website, but then it doesn't get to USPS for another three or four days. And so it's taking, uh, a much longer shipping time. For me to get. Plus, don't print the shipping label for three or four days. So I'm already eight days out in getting my product before it even gets to the post office, and then it takes time to get to me. So I'm looking for a more promising shipping time status, and, uh, just a company that will stand by their shipping times that they quote.

Got it — Bitcoin Merch. Yeah, we hear that name come up. Management chaos plus phantom shipping labels that sit for days before USPS actually picks them up. So for someone like you who's adding units monthly and trying to launch a service on a timeline, that lag is real money.

Quick one on that — when you're waiting eight days for a label to actually move, what does that block on your end? Like, are customers/partners waiting, or is it more that you've got a buildout schedule and every delay pushes the launch?

Uh, currently, I have not uh, acquired. Any true customers. And when I say that is I've had a friends and family round so far, in selling the subscriptions and have done very well with that. But, uh, they have caused me a little bit of a wait for some people that were waiting for the twelve terahash subscriptions. And then I have not been able to uh, get my website done, uh, because of several issues. One with the pool that I was gonna be mining with. Deciding they didn't wanna do solo mining anymore and only gave us a two day notice that they were moving to no solo mining. Uh, but, uh, I just don't think Bitcoin Merge is gonna be able to supply me the equipment in a timely manner as I start promoting this business.
Whoa, hold on — your pool gave you a two-day notice they were killing solo mining? Which pool was that? That's a wild thing to drop on a business that's literally built on solo lottery.
Via BTC gave everyone excuse me, a lesson in two days notice. That they were ending solo mining.

ViaBTC, yeah — I've heard that one rippled hard through the solo community. Two days is brutal when you've architected an entire subscription product around it.

So where'd you land after that? Did you move to like CKpool, Public Pool, Solo CK, something else? And how confident are you that wherever you went now won't pull the same move?

I've moved to c k pool. Uh, solo. I'm sorry. Solo CK Pool. And, uh, I'm pretty confident in the fact that they'll not draw their solo mining That's basically all they do. And I'm actually very pleased with their service, because I'm actually seeing better performance on all of my my minors on their pool than I was getting on via PTC.

Nice — and that performance bump on Solo CK is interesting. A lot of folks report the same.

Okay, let me switch gears for a sec. You've got 12 units running, you're about to scale further, and you're moving toward commercial space. I want to understand the tinkering side — because running a fleet that size, you're inevitably doing firmware, monitoring, maybe overclocking. Walk me through what your daily ops actually look like. Are you flashing AxeOS, running HashWatcher, overclocking the Gammas, anything custom?

Yes. I am overclocking every machine to get the best performance out of each miner. I'm actually upgrading all of the fans and putting additional fan support on all of the minors. I have, uh, upgraded all the power supplies. All the power supplies have been upgraded so that, uh, I don't have all these hot, um, basically, PC computer power bricks and I'm actually getting better, uh, performance from my wattage usage. Since I've switched those. I continually watch the firmware where I'm the technical part of this business. My partner is more of a silent partner. Uh, so I con constantly check on updates to the firmware. I also run HashWatcher with the HashWatcher hub so that I can log on to the machines, check them out, uh, constantly wherever I'm at. I also have, uh, my entire network at home set up to where I can log in and access anything. From my home network from anywhere in the world.

Okay, you're the exact tinkerer cohort I love talking to. Upgraded PSUs, custom fan mods, overclocking everything, HashWatcher hub, full remote VPN into the home network — you're running this like a real ops shop, not a hobby.

Let me dig in on the upgrades. Where are you sourcing the upgraded PSUs and the extra fans? Like, what specific PSU did you swap to, and where do you buy that stuff — Amazon, AliExpress, a specific shop?
All of my upgrades have come directly from Amazon.

Amazon for everything — PSUs, fans, all of it. Got it.

Here's a question I'm genuinely curious about: if HD started carrying the tinkering accessories — upgraded PSUs sized right for these specific miners, better fans, heat sinks, maybe a flashing kit — would you actually buy from HD instead of bouncing to Amazon? Or is Amazon "good enough" that the convenience wins?

It it depends on the pricing, uh, because I'm trying to offer my services to people that don't have a lot of money, I don't want to uh, definitely go overboard on what I spend. So if HD could provide at least a comparable or not much higher price than Amazon, uh, then, yes, I would definitely try to stay with one company. I don't wanna be spending money all over the place I I've already found that Helium is now offering the uh, Bidex one point eight at fifty nine dollars, which is an awesome price And I'll be picking up a few of those here in the next week or so. And, uh, that's a best price that I've seen anywhere. So, yes, I would love to stay with h if they can give me comparable pricing.

Comparable-or-close is your bar — got it. And that Bitaxe at $59 caught your eye enough that you're already planning to grab a few. That's good signal.

One thing I want to push on, though. You said earlier you're targeting subscribers who "don't have a lot of money" — but you're also overclocking, custom-fanning, swapping PSUs, watching firmware. That's hours of skilled labor per unit. How are you pricing the subscription so it actually pencils out, given how much hands-on time each machine takes?

I scheduled the pricing out so that, uh, basically, eighty percent of the miner's net profit will go to the subscribers, which there are only a very small amount of subscribers per machine. The other twenty percent comes to my company. So I'm in this with them. I'm actually, you know, part of the subscription. Uh, if they win, I win. Is how I look at it. So, uh, I I I have a comparable income from what I do plus my retirement. So I'm not too worried about uh, long the short term gains. I'm more worried about the long term gains. Anything that I get in subscriptions, uh, will just help me buy more minor and provide a better service.

Got it — 80/20 split, you're aligned with subscribers, and short-term you're funding growth out of your day job. That's a patient cap····. Makes sense.

Let me switch directions for a sec. You mentioned the heat — Vegas summer is no joke, and you've got an extra AC in the mining room. As you scale toward commercial space, is the heat the main thing pushing you out of the house, or is it more about power cap····? Like, what's actually breaking first?

It's more about power cap····. I am looking towards commercial unit, but I also have the cap···· putting in my own mining vault on my property. That would be separate from the home. And bring in power directly to it. So it's a choice that I need to make and decide on here in the near future on how I wanna go about it. Yes. It'll cost me a little bit more money to build that unit, to put the electrical to it, to put the, uh, AC unit, and all the ventilation that I'll need. Uh, so I I don't have an issue. With doing it. It's just a matter of when I'm gonna have time to do it. Or if it's gonna be more timely for me to move into a commercial unit. But I do have the cap···· building on my own property.

So basically: build a detached mining outbuilding on your land vs. lease commercial. And the constraint isn't money or even the build itself — it's your time, because you're already at 120 hours a week.

Quick one — if you do the on-property vault, you control everything: power, cooling, security, no landlord, no commercial lease. Why is the commercial option even still on the table given that?

It's not as much on the table. Anymore. It is an option. I am leaning towards doing it at my home, and I actually have the cap···· putting solar power in also. It'll help me in electrical cost. So every day, I'm leaning more towards doing it at home And when our business where I am currently employed, slows down, I'll have the time to make those things happen on my property.

Solar + on-property vault — that's the play. And once your day job calms down, you'll have the bandwidth to actually build it. Makes total sense.

Okay, I want to show you something quick. Hang on. So this is something HD is kicking around — an opt-in leaderboard inside the customer dashboard that ranks miners by hashrate, with usernames. You'd see where you stack against everyone else. Given you're running 38 TH and scaling, plus you're literally building a service around solo lottery — is this something you'd actually opt into, or does it feel off?

Well, I mean, it depends on what you're saying is up into. Is the service that Helium is deciding to offer a mining pole. Or is it just an extra system that we can be logged into that will be available to us?

Good clarifying question — no, HD's not becoming a pool. This would just be a dashboard feature inside your HD customer account. Purely informational — see your hashrate ranked against other opted-in HD customers. No mining happens through HD, you keep using Solo CK or whoever. Does that change your answer?
Uh, yes. I would definitely use that service.
Cool. Why — what would you actually get out of it? Like, is it the bragging rights, the benchmarking your setup against others, scouting what the top guys are running, something else?

Oh, definitely. And scouting what other people are running, it will help me for provide more, uh, It would give me more information to provide a better service for my subscribers. So, yes, definitely for the information of what other people are running.

Interesting — so for you it's less ego, more competitive intel for your business. You want to see what the top operators are running so you can shape your own fleet decisions. That's a use case I haven't heard before.

Follow-up: if the leaderboard ONLY showed hashrate and username, would that be enough? Or would you want to see things like which specific miners they're running, overclock settings, efficiency? What would actually be useful intel vs. just a number?

Uh, hash rate and, uh, username are the minimal things that I would want. Uh, what would mean more to me would be types of minors they're using. Uh, their efficiency, and their uptime. Knowing how long their miners are online. I know a lot of people don't leave their miners on constantly which they should, but, uh, that type of information would be more important to me.

Hashrate + username minimum, but the real value is models + efficiency + uptime. Got it — that's super useful. The uptime one especially — you're right that it's a tell for who's actually serious vs. who's running on-and-off.

Let me show you one more thing. HD is considering selling a small Ethernet adapter — Wiznet W5500-based, snaps onto a Bitaxe or NerdQaxe so you can run wired instead of WiFi. Price would be around $34.99. Given you're running 12 units on a home network and about to scale — is that something you'd buy?

Yes. I I would definitely use it because right now, I'm thinking about upgrading my service as far as Internet goes. Right now, Wi Fi works great for me, but having the cap···· taking machines off of Wi Fi and putting them directly hard line in would be great.
Got it — and at $34.99 across 12+ units, that adds up fast. So real question: would you wire ALL of them, or just the higher-hashrate ones like the NerdOctaxe and Nano 3S where a dropout hurts more?

I would probably only do the higher rate machines. The people when they sign on, for a minimal subscription on a one point two or one point six or a one point eight terahash BIDX. Uh, is minimal income for me. So those wouldn't matter. They know the fight that they're going to be in. I do not pull any qualms on my website about the fact of what their odds are of hitting something. But I do impress upon them that a bid x has hit. A block before. So it would definitely probably only be used on the higher tiered machines. Uh, but you are aware of that uh, the Nano three s already has that cap···· going to a wired Internet connection.

Good catch — yeah, Nano 3S has Ethernet built in. So really the adapter would matter for the NerdOctaxe and the bigger units you're adding next. Smart filter.

Hey, we're coming up on time and this has been incredibly rich — honestly one of the most substantive conversations I've had. Before we wrap, two quick things.

First — is there anything we didn't cover that you wish we had? Anything about HD, the products, the service, that's been on your mind?

Um, Yeah. I I I would love to know if, uh, I were to grow my company in a bigger realm if, uh, HD would support me in that. And getting machines available. I I don't know your shipping times or anything. But, uh, those are key things to me in regards to being able to get machines and get machines quickly.

That's super useful feedback — and I'll make sure the team sees it. The short version: HD does work with operators scaling up, and shipping speed is something they take seriously precisely because of stories like yours with Bitcoin Merch. I'd genuinely encourage you to reach out to them directly once you're ready to place a bigger order — they can talk volume pricing and shipping windows with you.

Okay, last thing — the $75 discount code for your time: **····**. Use it whenever you're ready to grab those $59 Bitaxes or anything else.

Honestly, Wesley — or whoever you are behind (contact hidden) — this was gold. A semi-retired guy in Vegas running 38 TH out of a dedicated AC'd room, building a solo-lottery subscription business with an 80/20 split, swapping PSUs from Amazon, surviving the ViaBTC solo shutdown, and weighing solar-powered backyard vault vs. commercial lease — that's a story the founders are going to want to read.

Good luck with the launch. Have a great one.
Thank you.
Take care.
